Sanjay: Heads-up: after kernel-selector patch (heuristics v2) we see a 10-15% tail latency regression on small-batch inference. nsys shows weird H2D spikes around kernel launch. Anyone else?
Emily: saw it in canary earlier this morning. spikes correlate with memcpy H2D (pageable) around KV cache misses. timeline looks like memcpyAsync -> kernel -> big memcpy stall.
Liam: can you paste a short nsys slice? might be pageable vs pinned fallback.
Sanjay: here's an excerpt from the nsys run I grabbed:```bash
nsys profile --stats true --output dmatrace ./run_infer.sh
# timeline excerpt
[  1.234s ] H2D memcpyAsync  1.2ms (pageable)
[  1.235s ] kernel: kv_lookup  0.5ms
[  1.236s ] H2D memcpyAsync  4.8ms  <-- big stall
```Also NVTX shows dma-probe events immediately before the big memcpy.
perf-bot: alert: pci-transfer-latency increased by 13% between commits abc123 -> def456.
Emily: my hunch: kernel-selector picked a larger-kernel path that allocates bigger transient CPU buffers. when pinned pool is exhausted, we fall back to pageable and the driver does on-the-fly pinning (cudaHostRegister), causing dma-probe and the stall.
Liam: that fits. we had a change in continuous-batching heuristics that increases prefetch size for small batches. if prefetch/peercopy tries to pin too many pages concurrently, you'll see exactly that.
Sanjay: repro details: small batches, seq_len=256, MEMPOOL_SIZE=64MB (defaults were 256MB). when I shrink the mempool the spikes appear; forcing pinned (FORCE_PINNED=1) removes spikes.
Emily: logs show "GPUDirect RDMA: fallback to staging buffer (pageable-to-pinned)" in the prefetch path. also seeing cudaHostRegister in the stack traces.
Liam: next steps I suggest: 1) nvprof/nvtx stack for a full trace, 2) bisect kernel-selector changes (def456 looks suspect), 3) add telemetry for cudaHostRegister counts.
Sanjay: quick repro command I used:
```bash
MEMPOOL_SIZE=67108864 FORCE_PINNED=0 ./perf_harness --batch 2 --seq 256 --iters 300
nsys profile --output /tmp/trace --sample=cpu,gpu ./perf_harness
```
Emily: I'm going to add a telemetry counter: runtime.pci_host_registers (count per minute) + dashboard alert if rate > 5/min. will also add a canary mempool size knob. ETA EOD.
Liam: I'll start a bisect on canary. initial spot-check: commit ghi789 doesn't touch the prefetch path, def456 does touch kernel_selector.c and changes "choose_variant_for_latency" heuristics.
Sanjay: if bisect confirms def456, I can push a revert to canary. prefer to revert temporarily rather than try to tweak mempool in prod immediately.
perf-bot: deploy: revert-kernel-selector pushed to canary at 1900509915; perf run started.
Liam: bisect step 3/7 — signs point to def456 as the cause (variant choice differs and triggers larger cpu staging).
Emily: added telemetry PR -> deploy staging. also added a quick unit test: simulate KV miss pattern with tiny pinned pool to ensure we catch on-the-fly pinning.
Sanjay: thanks. after revert I'll run the full perf harness and post numbers. if revert fixes it we'll plan a safer rework: make kernel-selector prefer variants that reuse pinned pools or allocate pinned buffers earlier (so we avoid cudaHostRegister in hot path).
Liam: another possible mitigation: make peercopy prefetch respect a max-pages threshold so it uses multiple smaller prefetch ops instead of one huge pin request.
Emily: noted. I'll add that as a follow-up ticket.
Sanjay: tl;dr: regression likely from kernel-selector heuristic change -> causes larger transient CPU buffers -> pinned pool exhaustion -> cudaHostRegister dma-probe -> H2D stall. Reverting on canary and adding telemetry + test.
Emily: +1. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: perf result: canary run (after revert) shows 11% tail latency improvement vs previous failing canary.
Liam: continuing bisect to be 100% sure, but this is looking like the root cause. will update thread when done.
Sanjay: great, thanks all. keep replies short — we'll coordinate follow-ups in the perf board.
